question: If the length of a resistor is doubled, what happens to its resistance, assuming all other factors remain constant?
solution:
The correct answer is __The resistance is doubled.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Resistance__ of a resistor is directly proportional to its length.
 
• If the length of a resistor is doubled, its resistance also doubles.
 
• Resistance is calculated using the formula R = ρL/A, where:
 
 
• ρ is the resistivity of the material.
 
• L is the length of the resistor.
 
• A is the cross-sectional area of the resistor.
 
 
• When length is increased but resistivity and area remain constant, resistance increases proportionally.
